analysis.title: TIC Data: Purchases of US Securities Remain Supported in September
key_insights: Foreign investors net purchased long-term US securities in September 2026 (preliminary US Treasury data), totaling $186.7bn versus a 6-month average of $202.6bn.
Foreign investors bought long-term US Treasuries, equities, corporate bonds and agency securities in September. Private investors drove net purchases across assets.
Net purchases of long-term US Treasuries were $80.8bn in September ($27.6bn official, $53.1bn private), against a 6-month average of $49.9bn.
India was the largest net buyer of long-term Treasuries in September, followed by Canada. France was the largest net seller.
By region, Europe and Asia were net buyers of long-term Treasuries and Latin America was a net seller.
Net purchases of US equities were $66.8bn in September ($7.97bn official, $58.8bn private), below the 6-month average of $107.9bn and well below August's $149.9bn.
Net purchases of long-term corporate bonds were $27.0bn in September versus a 6-month average of $36.6bn. Agency securities saw net purchases of $12.1bn.
US investors net purchased $31.4bn of foreign long-term securities in September: $38.0bn of bonds and net sales of $6.6bn of equities.
